name: Rehob
title: Father of Hadadezer, the Aramean king
summary: Rehob is primarily known as the father of Hadadezer, king of Zobah (an Aramean kingdom in Syria). He is mentioned in connection with David's wars against the Arameans. The name Rehob also appears as a place name and belongs to several people in the Old Testament, but the most prominent one is the father of Hadadezer.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as the father of Hadadezer
keyEvents.description: Rehob is identified as the father of Hadadezer, king of Zobah, when David defeated his army at the Euphrates River.

keyEvents.title: David's victory over Hadadezer, son of Rehob
keyEvents.description: David defeated Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, when Hadadezer went to restore his dominion at the Euphrates River. David took many prisoners and great spoils of war.

keyEvents.title: Spoils from Hadadezer, son of Rehob
keyEvents.description: King David dedicated the silver and gold he took from Hadadezer, son of Rehob, to the Lord, along with spoils from other defeated peoples.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The same account of David's victory over Hadadezer, king of Zobah, is retold in 1 Chronicles, although Rehob's name is not always explicitly mentioned there.

keyEvents.title: Rehob the Levite who sealed the covenant
keyEvents.description: Another person named Rehob is mentioned among the Levites who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah after returning from exile.
